verdict: The Laguna Phuket Marathon has earned its place as one of Thailand's longest-running resort races — a tropical full marathon that doubles as a destination weekend at a well-known Phuket resort complex. For 2027, five distances from a 2km kids' dash to the full 42.195km make it genuinely family-friendly, and the priority registration window for 2026 finishers suggests an organiser that rewards loyalty. The June date means heat and humidity will be the real opponent, not the course profile. Suits runners who want a resort-based race-cation with distance options for the whole family; serious PB chasers should look for a cooler-month event.

sections.heading: The Venue: Laguna Phuket, Bang Thao
paragraphs: The race is anchored at Laguna Phuket, a sprawling integrated resort complex on Phuket's northwest coast in Ban Bang Thao. [1] For runners travelling in, that means accommodation, race pack collection, start line, and post-race recovery all sit within the same resort footprint — a logistical advantage that removes the usual race-morning transport scramble.

Bang Thao itself is one of Phuket's longer beaches, running roughly 8km of sand, and the resort grounds are flat and manicured — expect a course that uses resort roads, beachfront paths, and connecting stretches rather than public highways. The 2026 edition and its predecessors have established a route template that the 2027 race is likely to follow.

sections.heading: The Distances: Five Options From Family Dash to Full Marathon
paragraphs: The 2027 edition offers five distances: a full marathon (42.195km), half marathon (21.098km), 10km, 5km, and a 2km fun run. [1] That spread makes it one of the more inclusive events on the Thai calendar — a family can arrive on Friday, run the 2km together on Saturday, and have one parent tackle the half or full on Sunday morning.

For serious marathoners, the full 42.195km is the headline distance, but the half marathon is arguably the sweet spot: long enough to feel like a proper race, short enough to finish before the tropical heat peaks.

sections.heading: Registration: Priority Window for Returning Runners
paragraphs: Registration for the 2027 race currently offers priority access to runners who completed the 2026 edition. [1] That's a smart retention move by the organiser — it rewards loyalty and gives returning runners an early chance to secure their spot before general entry opens to the public.

For first-time entrants, the priority window means waiting for general registration to open, which hasn't been announced yet. The official site at phuketmarathon.com is the place to watch. Given the resort setting and the race's established history, general entries are unlikely to sell out overnight, but the priority-window approach is a nudge to plan ahead rather than assume a last-minute sign-up will be available.

sections.heading: The June Factor: Heat, Humidity, and the Early Start
paragraphs: June in Phuket sits inside Thailand's southwest monsoon season — it's hot, humid, and can deliver short, sharp downpours, typically in the afternoon. Morning conditions are generally runnable, and the race will almost certainly flag off the full and half marathon in the pre-dawn hours to get the bulk of the field through before the sun climbs.

This isn't a race where you chase a PB unless you're specifically heat-trained. The resort setting and flat course profile keep things manageable, but the climate is the course's real difficulty. Hydration strategy and a conservative early pace matter more here than split discipline.

sections.heading: Should You Run It?
paragraphs: If you want a resort marathon that doubles as a Phuket holiday — with five distances to include the whole family — the Laguna Phuket Marathon is one of Thailand's most established options. The 2027 edition is set for 12 June at Laguna Phuket, Bang Thao, with priority registration currently open for 2026 finishers. [1]

But for runners who value a well-integrated resort race where accommodation, start line, and finish festival share the same postcode, it's worth a calendar spot.
